definitions.explanation: The essential or most important quality of something, especially an art, discipline, or tradition. Emphasizes the deepest, most fundamental aspect that defines its true nature.

examples.japanese: {武道|ぶどう}の{神髄|しんずい}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: To learn the essence of martial arts.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{修行|しゅぎょう}を{経|へ}て、ようやく{茶道|さどう}の{神髄|しんずい}に{触|ふ}れた。
examples.english: After many years of training, I finally touched upon the true spirit of the tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: この{一冊|いっさつ}には、{日本|にほん}の{伝統|でんとう}{芸能|げいのう}の{神髄|しんずい}がわかりやすくまとめられている。
examples.english: This book concisely summarizes the essence of Japan's traditional performing arts.

notes:
USAGE:
Used to describe the deepest, most essential quality of a discipline, art, philosophy, or tradition. Often appears in contexts involving mastery or deep understanding achieved through long study or practice. More literary and elevated in register than simply saying {本質|ほんしつ} (essence).
Similar to {真髄|しんずい} (same reading, different first kanji). Both words mean "essence" and are sometimes used interchangeably, but {神髄|しんずい} carries a slightly more spiritual or sacred nuance (using the kanji for "god/spirit"), while {真髄|しんずい} emphasizes truth and authenticity (using the kanji for "true").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神髄|しんずい}に{触|ふ}れる: to come into contact with the essence
- {神髄|しんずい}を{極|きわ}める: to master the essence
- {神髄|しんずい}を{伝|つた}える: to convey the essence

cross_references.description: Similar word with same reading but different nuance
